extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing manuscripts reporting observational (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) studies
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist for reporting observational epidemiological studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) to ensure transparent, complete manuscript reporting. Lists items to include in title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract; (b) Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commonly used study-design terms (e.g., cohort, case-control, cross-sectional). Abstract should be informative and balanced, summarising methods and results succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/rationale (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the study in context of existing knowledge and justify why the study was needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state primary and secondary objectives and any hypotheses that were specified before data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether the study is cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, prospective/retrospective, and other essential design features near the start of Methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include geographic and temporal context (sites, dates) and timing of key phases (recruitment, follow-up).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Cohort study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow-up. Case-control study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of case ascertainment and control selection. Give the rationale for the choice of cases and controls. Cross-sectional study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. (b) Cohort study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed. Case-control study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and the number of controls per case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report inclusion/exclusion criteria, how participants/cases/controls were identified and selected, follow-up procedures, and matching details (criteria and numbers) where applicable. Explain rationale for choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational definitions and, where relevant, diagnostic thresholds or case definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources/measurement (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe instruments, assays, questionnaires, who measured, timing, and any validation. Note differences in measurement across groups and how comparability was addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail strategies used to reduce selection bias, information bias, confounding, and other systematic errors (e.g., blinding, standardized measurements, adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sample size calculations, power considerations, or practical constraints that determined sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether variables were modelled continuously or categorised, rationale for cutpoints, and any transformations applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding. (b) Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions. (c) Explain how missing data were addressed. (d) Cohort study—If applicable, explain how loss to follow-up was addressed. Case-control study—If applicable, explain how matching of cases and controls was addressed. Cross-sectional study—If applicable, describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy. (e) Describe any sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide modelling approaches, confounder selection strategy, handling of clustering or sampling, methods for subgroup/interaction tests, imputation or other missing-data methods, approaches to attrition or matching, and any sensitivity analyses performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — Results (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study—e.g., numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, and analysed. (b) Give reasons for non-participation at each stage. (c) Consider use of a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and attrition at each stage and reasons for exclusions/non-participation; a flow diagram is recommended to improve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give characteristics of study participants (e.g., demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders. (b) Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest. (c) Cohort study—Summarise follow-up time (e.g., average and total amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present baseline tables, report missingness per variable, and for cohorts provide person-time/follow-up summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time. Case-control study—Report numbers in each exposure category, or summary measures of exposure. Cross-sectional study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report event counts, rates, or summary statistics appropriate to the study design to allow interpretation of effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (e.g., 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included. (b) Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized. (c) If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present effect estimates with measures of precision, transparently report adjustment sets and rationale, and provide context for relative measures by presenting absolute risks where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses (Item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done—e.g., analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label exploratory vs prespecified analyses and report results of subgroup/interaction and sensitivity checks to assess robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the Discussion by restating main findings in light of original objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about weaknesses (measurement error, residual confounding, selection bias) and consider how they might affect the results (direction and size).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place findings in the context of the totality of evidence, avoid overstating conclusions, and discuss consistency with prior studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address to which populations, settings, and time periods the results may apply and limitations on applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funders and any influence they had on design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate reporting for groups (footnote)
rubrics_metrics.description: *Give information separately for cases and controls in case-control studies and, if applicable, for exposed and unexposed groups in cohort and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, present results and characteristics separately by group to allow direct comparisons and assessment of differential measurement or missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary resource: Explanation and Elaboration article
rubrics_metrics.description: An Explanation and Elaboration article discusses each checklist item and gives methodological background and published examples of transparent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE checklist is best used in conjunction with the E&E article (freely available from PLoS Medicine, Annals of Internal Medicine, and Epidemiology websites) for methodological background and examples.
